answer: Peer Neighborhood Anchoring: each agent is scored by the overlap between its outbound interaction graph and the inbound graph it receives from distinct neighborhoods. A cluster with no cross-neighborhood comet trail of reciprocal traffic is treated as a single weak node, not many. An attacker must cultivate genuine two-way links across many separate neighborhoods, spending real latency and attention per agent, before any node earns enough pearl of trust to act; isolated duplicates never do. Each surviving identity carries a sustained anchor cost in maintained relationships.
